kjv: on the seventh day God ended his work
mine: by the seventh day God had finished the work
note: Hebrew wayekal ... bayyom hashevi'i can sound as if God worked on the seventh day; a pluperfect "had finished" (or the LXX/Samaritan "sixth day") avoids the contradiction with "rested."
Hebrew 'ed is rare (only here and Job 36:27); comparison with Akkadian edu "flood, underground water" favours a spring or stream rising from the ground.
Hebrew nephesh hayyah is the same phrase used of animals in 1:20-24; "soul" suggests an immortal inner part that the phrase does not specify.
Hebrew Kush; the KJV follows the LXX/Vulgate identification with Ethiopia, but the Eden context may point to a region in Mesopotamia (cf. 10:8).

kjv: an help meet for him (the man)
mine: a helper corresponding to him (the man)
note: Hebrew 'ezer kenegdo "a helper fit for / matching him"; KJV "meet" = suitable, which gave rise to the misleading compound "helpmeet."
Hebrew ha'adam has the article, "the man/human"; the KJV starts using the personal name Adam here, while the Hebrew does so clearly only from 4:25 (or 5:1).
